steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide, I'm coming! Stop playing the cello!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Are you trying to get yourself killed?!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That is something I've considered.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'll draw all the slugs over with the sound of my cello, and then... burn myself to ashes, along with them.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But now that you're here... I probably won't have a chance to do that anymore.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide, why...?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Ever since I was little, I knew there was something wrong with me.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The Infected who spent a lot of time around me... their sickness kept getting worse and worse.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: My grandpa and I were chased out of our home for it. We started wandering between villages.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I always thought, it wasn't all Infected people. That as long as they didn't spend too much time around me, they'd be fine.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But my grandpa's condition finally started to deteriorate, and that shattered my first illusion.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: After that, Hibiscus told us about the phenomenon of 'false recovery.' I've already caused such serious damage in the short time since I came to the Afterglow.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: If me living brings calamity to others, then I would rather die.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's not your fault!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: How is it not my fault?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ––Do you know about the Voice of Mundane?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Now that you mention it, I... think I'm finally starting to remember.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: About the Voice of Mundane, those who died in the experiment, the Witch King's remains... and you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I remember it all now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That's why none of this is your fault!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Witch King and his remains are to blame, as well as Gertrude – but you're innocent!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Thank you for reminding me that this isn't something I was born with. It was the foul product of an experiment.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I couldn't remember either until I heard the sound of your cello, so I should be thanking you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: 'But' what?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The situation has already spiraled out of control. I can't even mitigate the harm I cause anymore.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Besides, if the Gräfin's words are true, then my days are numbered. I might as well do something here...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why would I get myself tricked by Gertrude? Voices of the Mundane can be swapped out!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But mine is already corrupted... Even if I were to transfer it to your...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: We won't know until we try!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If you're already prepared to die, then what are you still scared of?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I don't want to hurt you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You can worry about that if something bad actually happens to me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Until then, let's make a wager.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Can you normally feel the melody of the Voice of Mundane?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Whether I'm performing or casting Arts, I can always vaguely feel the presence of the Voice... I know this shrill melody well by now, even though it's not at all mine.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Mine isn't shrill. If anything, it's gentle – Rather, I should say that it's so harmonious, almost to the point of being an empty void.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let's try our best to match the melodies we've experienced, and put them together.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Put them together...? But we don't have an audience.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, look at the audience all around us.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The Originium slugs?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Playing to Originium slugs the melodies that the old bastard left behind is quite fitting, if you ask me – humane, even.

a.text: As soon as the sounds of flute and cello intermingle, both men immediately recognize the problem.
There is hardly any consonance between their two melodies.
The flute's voice is urgent, manic, and harsh. It speeds up and slows down, as if filled with an urge to drag everything before it into the abyss.
The cello's voice is languid, melancholic, and hollow. Its rhythm remains constant, akin to a land ground down to nothingness by Catastrophe.
But the two brace themselves and persevere, continuing their duet that is not a duet.
The slugs surge forward like the tide.

Underneath a noxious sky, the two men whose lives have been twisted by their Voices of the Mundane continue their discordant duet, reading the score of a melody that they never knew existed in their minds, playing before an audience of Originium slugs.
The more Ebenholz follows this train of thought, the more he feels himself approaching the coda of the Voice of Mundane's melody.
He puts more force behind his breaths, while the sounds of Kreide's cello grow heavier and hollower.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Ebenholz, I...

a.text: Ebenholz lowers his head to look towards Kreide. Kreide's head has already begun to droop. His hand continues bowing, but the cello's sound becomes dimmer and dimmer, getting closer and closer to nothingness.
Suddenly, in this moment, Ebenholz seems to realize something.
So, he uses his remaining strength to blow one final sforzando.
Kreide also seems to be struggling, laboriously sawing at the thickest string on the instrument.
Their music spreads like an alarm bell.
The slugs that had been frantically rushing towards the pair of musicians suddenly retreat just as quickly, as if they have seen a predator.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide... Are you still with me...?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide, are you still awake?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: (Draws heavy breaths)

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: ...I'm awake.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: How's that? Can you still hear the melody of your Voice of Mundane?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: To be honest, it seems even clearer now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Sorry, I acted without thinking.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But on the bright side, we managed to drive away the Originium slugs––

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hold on...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide, what's wrong?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The new suit you bought for me––

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Oh good, it hasn't been soiled.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Probably doesn't smell too good though, right?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: True enough.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's fine. I bet you can't even imagine how much I reek right now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Speaking of which, this wouldn't be the first time I've gotten myself into this mess.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That time, a fire broke out not far from the Spire of Urtica. Instead of going to put out the fire, the Spire's attendants all rushed over to make sure I couldn't go anywhere.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: They were afraid you'd run away?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Afraid that I'd run away, afraid that I'd go into hiding, afraid that I'd die in that sea of fire...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: They worried about you dying?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Nearly all the windows in the Spire had Arts-enhanced bars and locks, just in case I tried to jump off.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I was a prized figurehead. If I went off and died, they wouldn't have been able to endure the consequences.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: In the end, the flames never reached the Spire, but I did get marinated in the smell of smoke.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I wore that smoke-soaked coat for a good half month and didn't take it off until the weather warmed.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That brings back old memories here as well.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: After my grandpa and I were run out of our old home, we started to wander between some of the more affluent villages.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Most people were pretty friendly to us, as long as we hid the fact that we were Infected.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I read in novels that during the harvest season, friendly villagers would prepare bratwurst and beer for the day workers at night so that they could eat and drink to their heart's content.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The friendly villagers threw some spare change at us and shooed us out of the village before nightfall, in fear that we'd steal things.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The not-so-friendly villagers prepared some rock-hard Schwarzbrot, and pointed weapons at us, intended to make us fall in line.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: One time, I was helping a villager out with some farm work.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It was really hot that day and I was dripping with sweat, so I wanted to loosen my clothes while nobody was around.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Right before I was about to take off my shirt, I heard a commotion not far away.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Grandpa rushed over and told me to run, saying that one of the workers rolled up his sleeves thinking nobody was watching, accidentally revealing the Originium crystals on his arm.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The villagers immediately threw him into an abandoned cellar and locked him up, and then set out to check everyone else, one-by-one.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: If not for Grandpa, I might've also died in that cellar.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Died–– They actually kill the Infected?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: They didn't need to, nor did they dare.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: All they had to do was wait for them to starve, crystallize, and explode...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hasn't there been a long-standing law to treat the Infected with dignity?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I never knew about a decree like that until I first set foot in a nomadic city.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm so sorry...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't know what to say.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: You have nothing to apologize for. You were also deceived by the Gräfin...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, what I mean is, if I had been a little braver back then... If I, if I had spoken up back then, maybe you wouldn't have had to––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Really, you don't have anything to apologize for.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Just as you said, the Voice of Mundane was made by man. The blame falls on those who sought to use the Voice of Mundane, not on you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I protected you in the manner I could...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Just like you're trying to protect me now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Thank you, Kreide.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Come, let's find Hibiscus and Herr Czerny... They'll know what to do, I'm sure of it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And then, we'll have that Voice of Mundane removed from you. You can thank me properly after that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let's go––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Kreide's condition is more or less stable. The reason he passed out most likely has to do with the poison.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: We've rescued a number of poisoning patients whose signs and symptoms largely match with Kreide's.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But on the subject of Kreide's future... the Countess probably didn't lie. Overall, his condition is on the edge of critical.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So, you'll help us, won't you?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I... want to trust the two of you, I really do.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But I need proof.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Even if it's circumstantial evidence, I need some objective facts to show that the Voice of Mundane isn't baseless speculation, but a part of an imminent plot––

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sir?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Where've you been? We've been looking all over for you!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Lies? Speculation?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Can you be a hundred percent sure that what you say is true?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: What you said to Kreide... Do you know that he almost died along with those Originium slugs because of your words?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz, is that true...?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Nods slightly)

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Had Ebenholz not found him first, you would've never seen him again!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I'm telling you, the Voice of Mundane is real. That I swear on my life!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I don't have time to explain it to you right now. I have work to do.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But, I need to...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You're among the most stubborn folk I've ever met.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Go to the lounge of the concert hall, and you'll understand everything.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Right, the concert hall!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Gertrude said she did something to Afterglow Hall to make it match with the Arts during the duet!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Alright, let's go right away–

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: There's also Czerny. Make sure you bring him as well, in case neither of you can convince the other.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I have to go now.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sir, you...
Ebenholz and Hibiscus trade glances.
They are both suspicious, but they are also running out of time.
